Byomkesh.description: The main detective, known as a 'truth-seeker', who investigates and solves mysteries.

Kamal Babu.description: A bank cashier who rents a room in Akshay Mondal's house and seeks Byomkesh's help; 'babu' is a respectful term for a gentleman or elder.

Akshay Mondal.description: The landlord of the house, later revealed to be a gold smuggler and murderer.

Harihar Singh.description: A hardened criminal and associate of Akshay Mondal, found murdered in the house.

Rakhal Sarkar.description: The police officer who assists Byomkesh in the investigation, respectfully addressed as Darogababu.

Satyawati.description: Byomkesh's wife, who asks him about his activities after the case is solved.

Bhuto.description: Kamal Babu's fierce mountain dog, used to guard the house.

Lohar Biscuit.description: The Bengali title of the story, meaning 'Iron Biscuit', referring to the iron cases used to hide gold.

Hindustan Park.description: A neighborhood in Calcutta (Kolkata), indicating the story's urban setting.

Keyatala.description: A locality in Calcutta where Byomkesh resides.

Central Bank of India.description: A major Indian bank where Kamal Babu works as a cashier.

Purulia.description: A district in West Bengal, India, from where Kamal Babu and his family hail.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, the capital of West Bengal and the main setting of the story.

Haridwar.description: A holy city in Uttarakhand, India, known for Hindu pilgrimages.

Hrishikesh.description: A sacred town in Uttarakhand, India, popular for pilgrimages and yoga.

Kundu Special.description: A reference to a special pilgrimage tour package, likely run by the Kundu travel agency.

muga.description: A type of silk produced in Assam, India, here referring to strong thread used to wrap the iron staff.

poppadum.description: A thin, crisp, disc-shaped Indian snack made from seasoned dough.

aubergines.description: Eggplants, commonly used in Indian cuisine and referred to as 'begun' in Bengali.
